title: Six Agent Harness Capabilities for Higher Model Performance | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA Labs open-sourced NOOA, an object-oriented agent harness that structures agents as single Python classes with typed methods and a self-curated SQLite memory store, hitting SOTA on SWE-bench Verified (82.2%), CyberGym L1 (86.8%) and ARC-AGI-3 (85.1%) at roughly half the token cost of comparison harnesses by passing tool results by reference instead of serializing them into context.

insights.claim: Harness design (how context is rendered, actions are executed, state is managed, and task completion is decided) can cause double-digit swings in benchmark results and significant differences in token cost even with the identical underlying model.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Model choice alone is an incomplete lens for evaluating AI agent capability or cost; investors and buyers assessing agent products should weight harness/orchestration engineering as much as underlying LLM selection.
insights.quote: Harness design alone can account for double-digit swings in benchmark results and significant differences in token cost, with the same underlying model.
insights.locator: Building a great AI agent isn't just about choosing the right models

insights.claim: NOOA (NVIDIA Labs Object-Oriented Agents) structures an agent as a single Python class: methods are capabilities, fields are state, docstrings are prompts, and type annotations are enforced contracts, with an LLM-driven loop completing any method whose body is an ellipsis at runtime while normal-bodied methods run as deterministic code.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: A code-first agent abstraction (vs. prompt templates/tool schemas/workflow graphs) lowers the engineering overhead of building and maintaining reliable agents, a structural advantage worth tracking against LangChain-style graph frameworks.
insights.locator: An agent is a Python object

insights.claim: Because NOOA agents are ordinary Python classes, agent development becomes traditional software development: agents can be diffed, code-reviewed, unit-tested, traced, versioned, and refactored by humans and by AI coding agents using existing software tooling.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Bringing agents into standard SDLC tooling (CI, code review, version control) reduces the operational risk premium enterprises attach to deploying agentic systems in production.
insights.quote: The payoff is that agent development becomes traditional software development.
insights.locator: An agent is a Python object

insights.claim: NOOA's architecture identifies six model-facing interface ideas said to drive agent performance: typed input/output instead of free text, pass-by-reference to live Python objects instead of serialized dumps, code as the action mechanism, programmable orchestration loops writable by developer or model, explicit typed object state instead of conversation-history-only state, and model-callable harness APIs for context and event history.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: This six-point checklist doubles as an evaluation rubric for competing agent frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, custom orchestrators) to assess how much headroom they leave on the table.

insights.claim: NOOA's long-term memory is a human-readable SQLite store the agent actively curates via model-callable tools (writing, querying, correcting records) rather than an automatic background summarization pipeline, with records carrying types, importance, tags, and typed relationships such as 'supports', 'contradicts', and 'derived-from' that form a knowledge graph rather than a flat log.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: A queryable, relational, agent-curated memory store is a differentiated architecture vs. vector-DB RAG or flat conversation logs used by most agent stacks, and could become a reusable component for enterprise agent memory products.
insights.quote: memory is a store the agent curates through model-callable tools
insights.locator: The agent curates its own memory

insights.claim: A background reflection pass consolidates NOOA's memory store by merging duplicates, linking related records, distilling episodes into insights, and pruning information no longer relevant, enabling agents to accumulate knowledge across sessions without retraining, stored in one inspectable, shareable SQLite file.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Session-to-session knowledge accumulation without retraining reduces the case for costly fine-tuning cycles in enterprise agent deployments where task context evolves over time.
insights.quote: A background reflection pass consolidates the store by merging duplicates, linking related records, distilling episodes into insights, and pruning information that is no longer relevant.
insights.locator: The agent curates its own memory

insights.claim: On the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, NOOA's memory subsystem alone improved RHAE score by +11.8 points versus the identical agent using file-based notes instead of the structured memory store.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Quantifies memory architecture as a standalone performance lever (+11.8 pts) separate from model choice, useful for isolating which agent-stack investments actually move benchmark outcomes.
insights.quote: the system improved RHAE by +11.8 points over the same agent with file-based notes
insights.locator: The agent curates its own memory

insights.claim: On SWE-bench Verified, NOOA reaches 82.2% accuracy with GPT-5.5, above the published leaderboard SOTA at submission time of 79.2%, and 79.8% with Opus 4.6, using a general-purpose 253-line agent with no benchmark-specific prompts.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: A 253-line general-purpose harness beating specialized SOTA coding-agent submissions suggests harness architecture, not benchmark-specific tuning, is becoming the bigger lever for coding-agent leaderboards.
insights.quote: NOOA reaches 82.2% with GPT-5.5 above the published leaderboard SOTA at submission (79.2%)—and 79.8% with Opus 4.6, using a general-purpose, 253-line agent with no benchmark-specific prompts.

insights.claim: On CyberGym L1, a real vulnerability-rediscovery benchmark, NOOA solves 86.8% of tasks with GPT-5.5 -- the top score among open-source agents and ahead of most leading closed-source systems -- run with network access blocked and a rule-based cheat check confirming results come from reasoning over code rather than looking up disclosed vulnerabilities.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: An open-source harness beating most closed-source cybersecurity agents on real vulnerability rediscovery is a signal that harness engineering can offset a closed-model/closed-system advantage, relevant to AI-driven vuln research and bug-bounty tooling markets.
insights.quote: NOOA solves 86.8% with GPT-5.5. The top-scoring open-source agent, ahead of the majority of leading closed-source systems.

insights.claim: On ARC-AGI-3, a single NOOA agent reaches 50.2% mean RHAE with GPT-5.5 and 85.1% with GPT-5.6-sol, both staying under $20 per game ($17.85 and $13.3 respectively), advancing the benchmark's score-cost Pareto frontier.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Sub-$20-per-game cost at 85.1% on an unsolved general-reasoning benchmark is a concrete cost/capability data point for anyone modeling inference spend on agentic reasoning workloads.
insights.quote: advancing the benchmark’s score–cost Pareto frontier at under $20 per game across the board ($17.85 and $13.3; scorecards: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6-sol).
insights.locator: Reaching 85.1% RHAE on ARC-AGI-3 for under $20/game

insights.claim: In ARC-AGI-3 competition mode under a two-hour cap, the GPT-5.6-sol NOOA fleet solved 19 of 25 unknown grid games in full while reaching 85.1% mean RHAE at about $13.3 per game.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Full-solve rate (19/25) is a stronger capability signal than partial-credit scoring alone, useful for gauging real-world reliability of agentic reasoning systems on novel tasks.
insights.quote: with 19 of 25 games solved in full
insights.locator: Reaching 85.1% RHAE on ARC-AGI-3 for under $20/game

insights.claim: With GPT-5.5, NOOA reaches 82.2% on SWE-bench Verified using 29 LLM calls and about 1.1M tokens per task, while comparison harnesses need 66 calls and 2.2M tokens to reach 78.2%, or 29 calls and 1.3M tokens to reach 78.6% -- parity or better accuracy at roughly half the token cost.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Roughly 2x token-cost efficiency at equal or better accuracy directly translates to lower per-task inference spend for any team running agentic coding workloads at scale.
insights.quote: NOOA reaches 82.2% on SWE-bench Verified using 29 LLM calls and ~1.1M tokens per task. The comparison harnesses need 66 calls and 2.2M tokens to reach 78.2%, and 29 calls at 1.3M to reach 78.6%.
insights.locator: Same performance, half the tokens and no context compaction

insights.claim: Because NOOA passes tool results by reference as live, typed, bounded Python previews instead of serializing them into the context window as text, it avoids needing context compaction or summarization even on frontier models with large windows -- median SWE-bench sessions peak at 22-72k prompt tokens against 200-400k available context, keeping transcripts append-only and cache-valid so prefill cache hits compound across the task.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Eliminating compaction/summarization passes is a reusable architectural trick other agent-framework builders and inference providers could adopt to cut both latency and token spend on long agentic sessions.
insights.quote: median sessions peak at 22–72k prompt tokens against 200–400k windows.
insights.locator: Same performance, half the tokens and no context compaction

themes.theme: Sandboxing and Security Validation of Agent Runs

insights.claim: NOOA's ARC-AGI-3 competition fleets run under layered sandboxing consisting of an in-process cell guard, a per-run OS privilege drop, end-to-end anonymization of game identities, and a kernel-enforced per-cell sandbox.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Multi-layer sandboxing for benchmark integrity is a template enterprises can borrow when running untrusted or self-modifying agent code in production or evaluation pipelines.
insights.quote: an in-process cell guard, a per-run OS privilege drop, end-to-end anonymization of game identities, and a kernel-enforced per-cell sandbox
insights.locator: Reaching 85.1% RHAE on ARC-AGI-3 for under $20/game

insights.claim: Red-team audits of both ARC-AGI-3 fleets -- 18 passes over the live GPT-5.5 run and a nine-scanner audit of the GPT-5.6-sol run, examining 13,335 and 10,107 logs respectively -- found no rule leakage, and NVIDIA pairs NOOA with its OpenShell secure runtime for production deployment.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Independently audited benchmark integrity (no leakage across ~23k logs) strengthens the credibility of NOOA's reported scores versus results that could be inflated by information leakage; OpenShell is a named product to watch for enterprise agent-security offerings.
insights.quote: Red-team audits of both fleets—18 passes over the live GPT-5.5 run and a nine-scanner audit of the GPT-5.6-sol run—found no leakage on any rule (13,335 and 10,107 logs examined).
insights.locator: Reaching 85.1% RHAE on ARC-AGI-3 for under $20/game

insights.claim: In internal NVIDIA vulnerability-discovery research, the validation pipeline is implemented as a single NOOA object with three deterministic gate methods (crash-or-no-crash verdict, crash-matches-vulnerability confirmation, reproduction rerun) that run as enforced typed code rather than prompt instructions the model might not follow, so a finding is accepted only when the code confirms it and the entire run is a single inspectable trace.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: Encoding verification as deterministic typed methods rather than trusting model instruction-following is a concrete pattern for reducing false positives in AI-driven vulnerability research pipelines, relevant to security tooling vendors.
insights.quote: a finding is accepted only when the code says so, and the whole run is a single trace we can inspect and test.

insights.claim: NVIDIA is releasing NOOA publicly as a research preview -- framework, capability tests, benchmark agents, code, data, and evaluation methodology -- positioning it as an open experimental surface meant to be inspected, challenged, and extended rather than a replacement for existing agent harnesses.
insights.speaker: Ricardo Silveira Cabral
insights.so_what: NVIDIA open-sourcing a competitive agent harness (not just models/chips) extends its platform strategy into the agent-software layer, potentially pulling developer mindshare and workloads toward NVIDIA tooling and, by extension, NVIDIA compute.
insights.quote: NOOA is available as an open experimental surface, not a replacement for existing harnesses.
insights.locator: A research preview for the open agent ecosystem
